interest: Shows Japan's cultural programs in occupied Asia, US monitoring of them, and Japanese Americans' precarious status in 1940 Japan.
overview: This file comprises U.S. State Department records from March 1940 and March 1943 filed under decimal classification 894.427, documenting Japanese cultural diplomacy, propaganda, educational reorganization, and related population policies during the early Pacific War era. The centerpiece is an extensive 45-page report compiled in January 1943 by the Division of Cultural Relations—drawing upon Federal Communications Commission (FCC) shortwave radio monitoring—that surveys Japan’s cultural offensive throughout the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere in 1942, encompassing language promotion, religious and school restructuring, scholar and student exchanges, bilateral agreements, and information control. Accompanying this report is the March 1943 diplomatic instruction dispatching it to the U.S. Embassy in Chungking, as well as a pre-war March 1940 memorandum assessing the demographic presence, social integration, and governmental exploitation of Japanese American dual citizens residing in Japan.
